<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To address the issues of poor topological connectivity and weak self-healing capabilities in wireless ad-hoc networks operating in complex power distribution cable channel environments, this study investigates methods for optimizing the reliability of such networks. Nodes are classified into three categories: core, relay, and terminal. A dynamic hierarchical topology is generated based on priority and environmental awareness, and a maintenance mechanism is established. The AODV routing protocol is improved to balance link quality and energy consumption during route selection. Adaptive frequency adjustment is used to avoid high-interference frequency bands in real time, while power control ensures communication reliability while conserving energy. With the aid of Turbo coding optimization, combined with real-time interference monitoring and early warning mechanisms, interference types are promptly identified, triggering network-wide anti-interference adjustments. The synergistic interaction of these three components ensures the reliable operation of wireless ad hoc networks in complex environments. Experimental results show that the proposed method maintains a network connectivity rate of over 98.5% even when interference intensity reaches −30 dBm. Compared to the baseline method, it reduces the data transmission bit error rate from a maximum of 0.019 to 0.0075 at a transmission distance of 100 meters, and, with 40 nodes per segment, reduces the link failure probability from a maximum of 8.9% in the comparison method to 0.8%, significantly enhancing the reliability of wireless ad hoc networks in the complex environment of power distribution cable ducts.</jats:p>
title: A reliability optimization method for wireless Ad Hoc networks in complex environments of power distribution cable channels
